design.batch_drain: peek heap[0][0] as event_t; heappop while heap[0][0] == event_t (exact float equality, same operator as legacy); process drained batch in pop order
design.entry: (event_time: float, driver_id: str, next_lap: int, next_age: int) tuple; comparison never reaches payload because driver_id is unique per live entry
design.initial_schedule: keep the roster-order initial scheduling loop byte-identical (it drives the RNG cursor), then heapify the live set
design.live_set_invariant: heap holds exactly the live pending set (one entry per unfinished driver with a scheduled lap); pop-then-push preserves the legacy dict invariant, so stale entries are impossible by construction and no generation metadata is needed
design.max_size: field size (~20); no growth, no compaction needed
design.payload_comparison: none: tuple order decides on (time, driver_id) only; next_lap/next_age never compared
design.steps_semantics: steps incremented once per drained batch, exactly as legacy increments once per sorted batch; termination bound identical
design.structure: heapq binary heap replacing dict nxt + per-iteration min/sorted/dictcomp/genexpr scan; finished dict and final (time, did) ordering untouched

equivalence_proof.batch_freeze: legacy freezes the batch list before processing any of its events; heap drain collects the identical set (all live entries with time == event_t) before processing any of them; newcomers wait for the next iteration in both
equivalence_proof.no_stale: legacy nxt holds at most one entry per driver (dict keyed by did; pop on process, overwrite on reschedule); heap pop-then-push preserves exactly one live entry per unfinished driver, so no stale entry can exist and none may execute
equivalence_proof.order: legacy batch is explicitly sorted by driver_id; heap pop order over (time, did) tuples is driver_id-ascending for equal times by the heap invariant; both consume the RNG cursor in that identical order
equivalence_proof.strictly_greater_reschedule: t_new = event_t + lap_time with lap_time > 0 enforced (non-finite or <= 0 returns False); magnitudes (~1e2 s laps over ~1e4 s races, ulp ~1e-12) make float addition strictly increasing, so a rescheduled event can never rejoin the batch being processed in either implementation
equivalence_proof.termination: per-batch steps counting and the not-pending break are preserved one-for-one (heap emptiness <=> no pending)

feasibility_gate: A_EXACT_ORDER_CONTRACT_PROVEN: tie rule is explicit in code (sorted driver_id strings), dict/insertion order provably irrelevant, reschedule strictly greater, single live entry per driver; heap key (time, driver_id) with frozen-batch drain reproduces legacy exactly with no additional metadata

float_specials.infinities: impossible: lap_time must be finite (else schedule returns False) and race times are finite sums
float_specials.minus_zero: no -0.0 possible: all event times are positive race-clock sums (~1e2-1e4 s); +0.0/-0.0 would compare == and break by driver_id identically
float_specials.nan: impossible: non-finite lap_time returns False; r3/mu finiteness raises; no NaN can enter the queue

rescheduling.cancellation: none: entries are popped on processing, never cancelled while pending
rescheduling.frequency: every processed non-terminal event reschedules exactly one successor (or sets ok=False)
rescheduling.multiple_pending_per_driver: impossible: nxt is keyed by driver_id with pop-then-overwrite
rescheduling.retirement: no retirement/DNF events exist in this kernel (docstring: never simulates DNFs); invalid trajectories arise only from schedule returning False
rescheduling.same_timestamp_reschedule: impossible (strictly greater, see proof); batch freezing additionally isolates the in-progress batch in both implementations
rescheduling.terminal: driver reaching scheduled laps records finished[did] and schedules nothing further; finished drivers are excluded from subsequent selection in both implementations

semantics.A_event_representation: tuple (event_time: float, next_lap: int, next_age: int) stored as nxt[driver_id]; event_time = time_s[did] + lap_time
semantics.B_queue_representation: plain dict nxt keyed by driver_id (at most one live entry per driver) plus finished dict; no heap, no versioning
semantics.C_insertion_order: initial fill iterates base_pace (roster order = initial_state.drivers order); reschedule overwrites nxt[did] in place (dict keeps original position) or appends at end after a pop
semantics.D_selection_rule: each while-iteration rebuilds pending = {did: v for did, v in nxt.items() if did not in finished}; event_t = min(v[0] for v in pending.values()); batch = sorted(did for did, v in pending.items() if v[0] == event_t); processes the batch one at a time
semantics.E_tie_rule: exact float equality (v[0] == event_t) then ascending driver_id string order via sorted()
semantics.F_dict_insertion_order: does NOT contribute: min() over values ignores order; the tied batch is explicitly re-sorted by driver_id
semantics.G_driver_iteration_order: contributes ONLY to initial scheduling order (roster order), which drives the per-sim RNG cursor for first-lap draws; within-batch processing order is sorted driver_id, not iteration order
semantics.H_min_receives: a generator expression over mapping values projected to [0]: min(v[0] for v in pending.values())
semantics.I_sorted_sorts_by: driver_id strings only (lexicographic ascending); the generator yields dids, no key function
semantics.J_stable_sort_relied_upon: no: driver_ids are unique so stability is unobservable; final race order sorted(finished, key=(time, did)) likewise has unique keys
semantics.K_event_time_type: float (float race clock plus float lap time)
semantics.M_same_timestamp_reschedule: no: lap_time > 0 strictly enforced (schedule returns False for non-finite or <= 0), so every rescheduled event is strictly later than the event just processed
semantics.N_simultaneous_processing: one-at-a-time in driver_id order within a batch list frozen before the first of them is processed
semantics.O_queue_mutation_between_ties: yes (pop processed entry, push rescheduled successor) but the in-progress batch list is already frozen and successors are strictly later, so they cannot join it

simultaneous_events: processed one-at-a-time in driver_id order from a batch list frozen before processing begins; queue mutations between tied events cannot affect the in-progress batch
